Messages.Author: Orpheus
Messages.Body:
I have already said in another thread what bothers me with the new vampires,
but it went mostly unnoticed in the general remarks on the new expansion.

Of course, there is G4 in itself, but well, what's done is done.

But I find 2 things very annoying / worrying :

1) The old "formula" doesn't seem to stick anymore !

In other terms : the new vampires (no matter their group) seem much stronger
than their predecessors.

It looks like specials, titles and sometimes out-of-clan disciplines don't
count as they used to !!

Examples :

- Ladislas Toth : 7 Cap, all 3 disciplines in sup + For ; would be the equal
of Eugenio Estevez (cost one more, has DOM) but he also has 2 votes !
- Celeste Lamontagne. As good as Raven (and she was good !)costwise, except
she has 2 specials (both cornercase, but it can make a difference)
- Spider : 6-cap, 2 inf and 2 sup (all "in-clan" and useful) + "steal a
weapon", and the oh-too-horrific blood burning condition (gotta block him,
then survive...)
- Mustafa, the Heir : 6-cap, 5 "points" of in-clan discipline + an
out-of-clan, 2 votes, and a cornercase special weakness (older toreador,
don't even have to play him with votes...)
- Shawnda Dorrit : Monstruous !!! All these disciplines and potentially 3
votes... Yeah, I know, Sela was very good too. But her inf Cel was worse
than Shawnda's inf Pot in most decks. And you don't have to make new
monsters just because there were some old ones...
- Guillermo : another 6-cap with 6 points of disciplines + a nifty special.

Etc, etc.

If the new vamps are going to get better and better, they will render the
old ones obsolete, and that can't be good for competitive play.

Another gut feeling about many of these "specials" is that they have a
randomness I don't like : it can make your minion very powerful or
unplayable depending on what is played at the table. And this I don't like a
bit.

2) Let's remake the old combos all over again !

I was very, very disappointed to see that G4 didn't even have that one good
argument : "they will open new combos, different from the previous ones".

We could have gotten some new out-of-clan possibilities, reaching into new
territories of inventiveness. Instead, what do we get ?

- another !Ventrue with Obt (sup).
- another !Brujah with Obt
- 2 new Ravnos with Pot

etc, etc.

Why ??? :-(

If you have to make vampires for the "old combos", one more in G3 couldn't
be bad. One more !Tore with For would have at last allowed some new variants
(2 just aren't enough). I don't think a 10-Cap friend for Quentin would have
made the !Ventrue more fearsome voters than any other clan (say, Lasombra or
Ventrue / Obf)...

If it is deemed "unbalancing, why not go for a new combo ? Why wouldn't the
G4 !Ventrue go for Obf, the G4 Ravnos get more Cel, etc ?

Part of what made G3 interesting was the novelty : the Ventrue had less
titles but more stealth, and the old ones still are played for that reason.
Same goes for lots of cammies : the Tores had Masika, Anson...

Printing clones of existing vamps is a waste of paper and money.

Printing clones, but better costwise, is the worst thing that could happen
to my favourite game in long-term.

The more I see the more I think I'll stick to my decision concerning (not
buying anymore) G4 ; but I'd like the game to stay challenging and balanced
for the "old" vamps.

Time will tell.

What do YOU think ?

--

Orpheus

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Orpheus wrote:

> 1) The old "formula" doesn't seem to stick anymore !

There was a formula in Jyhad. That formula changed in the original Sabbat
expansion (to where out of clan disciplines cost half and some special
abilties became much cheaper). When the game came back to life, the formula
was adjusted to something in the middle of the two--out of clans no longer
cost half, but some special abilities (like +1 bleed and +1 strength) cost
less than they did in Jyhad. And vampires of different capacities got more
stuff than in Jyhad. But the new set looks like it is using the same formula
as used for Black Hand, Anarchs, and Camarilla.

Picking some random vampires:
-Petra (5) OBF, ANI, aus = (+5). 2 highly conditional advantages, apparently
free (as 5 pointers get 5 points of stuff). Yeah, she seems a tad
overpowered compared to, like, Amelia. But only by virtue of some highly
conditional, if not corner case, specials.

-Skidmark (5) OBF, FOR, pot, aus = (+6). Significant disadvnatge (-1). Up to
code.

-Guillermo Arsuaga (6) POR, CEL, for, aus (+6). Limited advantage. Slightly
over the 6 points given to a 6 point vampire. Only very slightly.

-Faha al-Zawab'a (4) pre, for, cel (+3). Up to code.

-Hector Trelane (5) THA, AUS, nec, dom (+6). Minor advantage. Very
significant disadvantage. Seems even.

-Marcel de Breau (9) PRE, POT, CEL, pro, ani (+8). Arch Bishop (+1). +1
bleed (+1.5). Conitional advantage. +/-11 points on a 9 point guy. I think
the current formula (i.e. Camarilla+) gives 9 and 10 point vampires capacity
+2 points in stuff. Up to code.

If you keep going, you'll find that most of the vampires in this set fit the
standard introduced in Camarilla. If the new vampire designes are guilty of
anything, it is being extra liberal in rounding down half points here and
there to give vampires fun, but generally corner case, limited special
abilities.

>
> In other terms : the new vampires (no matter their group) seem much stronger
> than their predecessors.
>
> It looks like specials, titles and sometimes out-of-clan disciplines don't
> count as they used to !!

It looks to me like titles still cost .5 per vote; +1 bleed costs 1.5; out
of clan disciplines still cost normal. Again, if anything, there seems to be
liberty taken with rounding down the odd half point here and there spent on
weird, corner case specials.

>
> Examples :
>
> - Ladislas Toth : 7 Cap, all 3 disciplines in sup + For ; would be the equal
> of Eugenio Estevez (cost one more, has DOM) but he also has 2 votes !

7 and 8 point guys get cap+1 point of stuff in Camarilla. Up to code.

> - Celeste Lamontagne. As good as Raven (and she was good !)costwise, except
> she has 2 specials (both cornercase, but it can make a difference)

Again, if she is overpowered at all, it is by virtue of her having, like,
5.5 of abilities rounded down. Her two specials are either *very* corner
case (werewolf) or farily limited.

> - Spider : 6-cap, 2 inf and 2 sup (all "in-clan" and useful) + "steal a
> weapon", and the oh-too-horrific blood burning condition (gotta block him,
> then survive...)

So he has 6 in disciplines, a limited special (+) and a limited disadvantage
(-). Very even.

> - Mustafa, the Heir : 6-cap, 5 "points" of in-clan discipline + an
> out-of-clan, 2 votes, and a cornercase special weakness (older toreador,
> don't even have to play him with votes...)

So he has 6 in disciplines, a point in votes, and a balancing disadvantage.
Not a likely to come up disadvantage, but certainly very debilitating if it
does come up. Even.

> - Shawnda Dorrit : Monstruous !!! All these disciplines and potentially 3
> votes... Yeah, I know, Sela was very good too. But her inf Cel was worse
> than Shawnda's inf Pot in most decks. And you don't have to make new
> monsters just because there were some old ones...

Umm, wha? a 6 with 5 points of disciplines and possibly 3 votes (I suspect
that Priscus is costed at less than 3 votes--probably 1 point instead of 1.5
votes. Yeah, usually it is 3 votes, but sometimes it is zero votes).

> - Guillermo : another 6-cap with 6 points of disciplines + a nifty special.

See above. gain, it looks like these vampires occasionally get a free
conditional special abiltiy tacked on due to a rounding down of fractional
point. I can live with this.

> If the new vamps are going to get better and better, they will render the
> old ones obsolete, and that can't be good for competitive play.

The extra, minor special abilties here and there are hardly going to
obsolete anyone. And they cartainly aren't going to obsolete the higly
overpowered, pre-existing Sabbat vampires that didn't render anyone obsolete
either.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Orpheus wrote:

> I wasn't aware that the formula changed with the capacity. Still, some
> vampires in my list seem too good to be true. I'll admit Peter's theory that
> on the whole they "forgot" half a point here and there. It can make a
> difference, though.

Yeah, as far as I am aware, the "current" formula (from CE on) is something
like:

Cap 2-4: capacity-1 points of stuff.
Cap 5-6: capacity points of stuff.
Cap 7-8: capacity +1 points of stuff
Cap 9-10: capacity +2 points of stuff

Disciplines cost 1 point per level.
Votes cost .5 per vote. Priscus seems to cost 1 point.
+1 bleed or +1 strength costs 1.5
+1 stealth or +1 intercept costs somewhere in 1-2 point range

In the Jyhad set, the costs seemed to be similar, but:

Cap 5-8: capacity of stuff
Cap 9-10: capacity +1 points of stuff

+1 bleed and +1 strength cost 2 points.

In the Sabbat set, the costs were similar to the Jyhad set, except:

+1 bleed and +1 strength seemed to cost 1 point.
Out of clan disciplines seemed to cost half as much as in clan.

So certainly, many CE+ vampires are going to totally outclass similar Jyhad
vampires (but in turn, they might be outclassed by Sabbat vampires)--for
instance, most of the mid capacity Toreador from the Jyhad set are awful
(Adrianne and the two 7 pointers are total trash) compared to anything
anywhere.

It looks, again, as if the Gehenna vampires are *slightly* over the power
curve in some instances, but this is mostly due to the designers being
willing to add corner case specials for free. But they have been doing that
since CE anyway. I don't think this is going to obsolete anything (well,
except the very under the curve Jyhad vampires, like Adrianne and Zack
North). Overall, I don't think there are any vampires in the set that are
over the top in the way that Jimmy Dunn, Ian Forestall, or even Anvil are.
But there also don't seem to be any way under the curve vampires like poor
ol' Judah and Nakova.

I don't think it is problematic that they are willing to push vampires up a
little bit by virtue of adding "free" special abilties that are fairly
limited--I mean, yeah, if 4 point vampires started having 2 superior
disciplines and no disadvantage across the board, that would be a problem.
But that Petra gets aggrivated hand damaga against theBaali for free doesn't
strike me as a problem at all.
